title: Character tangent weights and positive rays for internal group actions
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $S,H$ be group schemes over $F$ [def-sc-group-scheme], with an internal action of $S$ on $H$ (a morphism $S\times_F H\to H$ satisfying unit and associativity). The action acts by group automorphisms when $s\cdot(xy)=(s\cdot x)(s\cdot y)$ on every test $F$-scheme; the action of $s^{-1}$ gives its inverse. For a subgroup inclusion $j:K\to H$ [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], stability means that for every test scheme $W$, $s\in S(W)$ and $x\in K(W)$, $s\cdot j(x)$ is in $j(K(W))$. A character is a group-scheme homomorphism $\chi:S\to\mathbf G_m$, where $\mathbf G_m$ is [def-sc-gm-ga]. Use the tangent space $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}(H)$ and its actual dual-number tangent points $v_\epsilon$ of [sk-d-tangent]. For $s\in S(F)$, extend $s$ constantly to $F[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$; evaluate $\chi(s)\in F$ on the Laurent coordinate $t$. Define $E_\chi=\{v\in\mathfrak h:s\cdot v_\epsilon=(\chi(s)v)_\epsilon\text{ for all }s\in S(F)\}$ and $\mathfrak h_\chi=\operatorname{span}_F(E_\chi)$. When the action is by group automorphisms, $E_\chi$ is already a vector subspace; when $F$ is algebraically closed and $S$ is a split torus these are precisely the usual character weight spaces, since $S(F)$ is Zariski dense in $S$. Characters are written multiplicatively, so define $R_\eta=\{\chi:\chi^m=\eta^n\text{ for some }m,n\in\mathbf N_{>0}\}$, and $V_\eta=\sum_{\chi\in R_\eta}\mathfrak h_\chi$, the subspace underlying the direct sum of the distinct character weight spaces in that setting.
